references.text: Joseph's interpretation of Pharaoh's dream: Seven years of great abundance will come upon all Egypt, followed by seven years of famine. Verse 53 shows the fulfillment of this prophecy.
Describes the seven abundant years when the land produced crops in abundance, and Joseph gathered large amounts of grain – the context leading up to verse 53.
After the seven good years ended (v. 53), the seven years of famine began as Joseph had predicted, and the famine spread over all lands.
The psalmist refers to how God brought famine upon the land and sent Joseph ahead, as part of God's plan of salvation for Israel in Egypt.
Amos describes famine as a tool of God, which parallels the famine in Egypt that followed the seven good years.
Both verses mark respectively the beginning and the end of the seven years of abundance in the same prophetic narrative.
The verses illustrate the connection between the prophecy of hunger (v. 30) and its actual occurrence after the end of the abundance (v. 53).
The verses describe respectively the execution and conclusion of the seven years of abundance in the same historical sequence.
The link shows how the storage proposed in v. 36 became necessary when the abundance ended in v. 53.
